root_cause.text: io_uring’s io_poll_get_ownership() incorrectly treated the req->poll_refs bitfield/flag counter as a signed int, so setting the high-bit IO_POLL_CANCEL_FLAG made atomic_read(&req->poll_refs) negative and bypassed the slowpath threshold check.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (unlikely(atomic_read(&req->poll_refs) >= IO_POLL_REF_BIAS))` to `if (unlikely((unsigned int)atomic_read(&req->poll_refs) >= IO_POLL_REF_BIAS))`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that because `atomic_read()` returns signed `int`, `IO_POLL_CANCEL_FLAG (BIT(31))` made `poll_refs` negative, causing the `>= 128` check to always fail and the slowpath to never be taken.

intent_record.what: The condition in io_poll_get_ownership() was changed to cast atomic_read(&req->poll_refs) to unsigned int before comparing it against IO_POLL_REF_BIAS.
intent_record.how: This makes the threshold comparison use unsigned semantics, preventing negative signed values from being treated as smaller than IO_POLL_REF_BIAS and ensuring the slowpath is taken correctly when poll_refs contains high-bit flag or wrapped values.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the ownership slowpath threshold check using atomic_read(&req->poll_refs) as a signed int. Because poll_refs also contains the high-bit IO_POLL_CANCEL_FLAG, setting that bit can make the signed value negative, causing the >= IO_POLL_REF_BIAS check to fail and incorrectly bypass slowpath ownership handling.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the relevant ownership logic in `io_poll_get_ownership()` and the added slowpath/flag handling. The root cause was that `req->poll_refs` was treated as a signed int, so setting `IO_POLL_CANCEL_FLAG` (`BIT(31)`) could make `atomic_read(&req->poll_refs)` negative and thereby bypass a threshold check. In this commit, the code already contains the fix: `io_poll_get_ownership()` now checks `if (unlikely(atomic_read(&req->poll_refs) >= IO_POLL_REF_BIAS)) return io_poll_get_ownership_slowpath(req);`, and the representation was changed so `IO_POLL_CANCEL_FLAG` remains `BIT(31)` but a separate `IO_POLL_RETRY_FLAG` is introduced as `BIT(30)`, with `IO_POLL_REF_MASK` reduced to `GENMASK(29, 0)`. The new slowpath avoids blindly incrementing when refs are elevated: `v = atomic_fetch_or(IO_POLL_RETRY_FLAG, &req->poll_refs); if (v & IO_POLL_REF_MASK) return false; return !(atomic_fetch_inc(&req->poll_refs) & IO_POLL_REF_MASK);`. This is exactly the robust handling described by the fix commit message and prevents the vulnerable construct of relying on a signed threshold comparison that can be defeated by the high cancel bit. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent in this version, and the fix is present.
